title: The Last Machine Again
premise: Mara Ashgrove smuggles memories between the warring fleets of Ceres and Ganymede, trading in other people's pasts while keeping none of their own. When a manifest lists a ship that never flew under a name Mara invented years ago, they discover their forged identity was used to broker a false peace treaty—one that both fleets believe the other signed. To keep two armadas from annihilating each other, Mara must impersonate the ghost they created, recover the original memory that proves the truth, and finally choose whether to remain invisible or become someone real. In the end, Mara broadcasts their own stolen childhood to both fleets, shattering the lie but forging a fragile truce built on shared memory rather than shared fear.
about_author: R. M. Underhill is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing customs manifests before turning fiction, and it shows. They live somewhere with unreliable gravity and write about people who carry too much of other people's pasts.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Mind
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A routine smuggling run through Ceres customs: encrypted memory chips hidden in coolant lines, bribed inspectors, a nervous client paying in ration scrip. We learn Mara's rules—never open what you carry, never be remembered. The beat is competence masking loneliness; Mara goes home to an empty berth and deletes the day's logs out of habit.

chapters.title: The Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A dockside contact shows Mara an intercepted manifest: the Perpetua, registered under 'Ashgrove, M., captain'—a ship class retired before Mara was born, on a route no one flies. Mara's forged identity has been used by someone else. Fear arrives cold; the beat is the first crack in invisibility.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Silence
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, with interludes from a Ganymede signals officer, Ivo Renk. Background on the Ceres–Ganymede split: twelve years of cold war since the Armistice of Halcyon Reach, which everyone remembers signing but no one can produce. Mara realizes the peace may rest entirely on documents—and memories—they never wrote. Beat: dread deepening into purpose.

chapters.title: What the Client Bought
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Tracing the memory chip sold three years ago that matches the Perpetua's registry date, Mara finds the buyer: a dead broker's estate, now controlled by Ceres intelligence officer Captain Sefa Okonjo. Okonjo knows someone will come asking. Beat: hunter and hunted circling politely over tea neither drinks.

chapters.title: The Name I Made
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Flashback woven through present interrogation: how young Mara, stateless after the Belt purges, fabricated the Ashgrove identity from a dead courier's files. Okonjo offers immunity for cooperation; Mara lies beautifully. Beat: the cost of a constructed self—the forgery fits better than the face.

chapters.title: Ivo Hears Ghosts
chapters.summary: Ivo Renk's POV. On Ganymede, Ivo decodes a transmission referencing the Perpetua and reports it up the chain—straight into a cover-up. His superior orders him to forget it; instead he copies the file into his own head, using the same smuggling tech he's supposed to interdict. Beat: a dutiful man choosing curiosity over obedience.

chapters.title: Running the Long Route
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Fleeing Ceres space, Mara takes the slow smuggler's corridor through debris fields, escorted reluctantly by old friend and fence Dessa Voss. Along the way they recover a fragment of the original Armistice memory—a child's-eye recording of the signing, apparently authentic. Beat: hope arriving like contraband, fragile and hot.

chapters.title: The Memory That Lies
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Analyzing the fragment with Dessa, Mara finds seams: the signing scene is edited, spliced from at least three sources. Someone manufactured the peace—or manufactured its collapse. Either way, whoever holds the master edit holds both fleets. Beat: vertigo; even history is smuggled goods.

chapters.title: Okonjo's War
chapters.summary: Okonjo's POV. Aboard her flagship, we see her motive: she helped forge the Armistice as a young officer to prevent a war her side would lose, and has maintained the lie for twelve years. Now the Perpetua leak threatens exposure, and she decides Mara must be silenced or owned. Beat: sympathetic antagonist; corruption as caretaking gone rigid.

chapters.title: Ganymede's Leash
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo is caught with the copied file and given a choice: prison or infiltration—find the smuggler named Ashgrove. He accepts, telling himself he'll judge the truth first. Beat: reluctant hound, quiet shame, the theme of belonging bought at the price of betrayal.

chapters.title: The Station of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. At neutral station Vesper's Rest, Mara seeks the Broker, the archivist who sells provenance, not goods. The Broker reveals the master edit exists and is stored—in a human mind, wiped and re-embedded, currently living as an anonymous dockworker. Beat: revelation plus moral horror; a person became a filing cabinet.

chapters.title: The Man Who Was a Treaty
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara finds the dockworker, Tomas Hale, who remembers nothing but dreams of a signing room every night. Earning his trust slowly, Mara must decide whether extracting the memory will destroy what's left of him. Beat: tenderness against urgency; Mara sees their own future in him.

chapters.title: Extraction
chapters.summary: Dessa's POV. In a borrowed clinic, Dessa performs the extraction while Okonjo's agents close on the station. Tomas survives but comes out hollowed, whispering coordinates instead of words. Mara gets the master edit—and a debt they intend to repay. Beat: triumph soured immediately by cost.

chapters.title: What the Edit Shows
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The full memory reveals the truth: there was no treaty. Both fleets' leaderships independently commissioned the same forgery to buy time, and the edit was the only copy binding them to pretend. Okonjo wasn't corrupting power; she was its janitor. Beat: moral inversion—Mara's enemy becomes the lie's most faithful prisoner.

chapters.title: Ivo Finds Ashgrove
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Tracking Mara to Vesper's Rest, Ivo confronts them—and instead of arresting them, asks to see the edit. What he learns breaks his chain of command and his certainty. He defects, bringing Ganymede fleet codes. Beat: alliance formed not on trust but on shared evidence.

chapters.title: Both Fleets Move
chapters.summary: Okonjo's POV, alternating with Ganymede command. The Perpetua leak reaches both admiralties; hardliners on each side declare the armistice void and begin mobilizing. Okonjo races to contain it, ordering Mara's capture alive. Beat: clock ticking, chapters shortening, stakes going planetary.

chapters.title: The Broadcast Problem
chapters.summary: Mara, Ivo, and Dessa plan. Broadcasting the raw edit won't work—each fleet's filters will flag it as enemy propaganda. The only format both sides trust is a verified personal memory, unedited, from someone both fleets have reason to believe. Mara realizes the only candidate is themselves. Beat: the smuggler must finally smuggle something of their own.

chapters.title: Recovering the Child
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. To broadcast authentically, Mara must unseal their own suppressed past: the purge of their home habitat, witnessed as a child, stored so long it has fossilized. The recovery session nearly unmakes them; Dessa anchors them through it. Beat: the book's emotional core—memory as wound and as proof of personhood.

chapters.title: Halcyon Reach
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. Both fleets converge on the old armistice site for what each believes will be a decisive strike. Okonjo, having read the edit herself via a leaked copy, makes her choice: she lets Mara's ship through the blockade instead of firing. Beat: climax assembling; enemies choosing, one by one, not to pull triggers.

chapters.title: The Truth, Out Loud
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. From a crippled relay barge between the two fleets, Mara broadcasts their own recovered memory interleaved with the master edit—childhood terror and forged signatures braided together, undeniable because it costs the teller everything. Silence falls across both fleets. Beat: catharsis; visibility as sacrifice.

chapters.title: After the Lie Dies
chapters.summary: Ivo's and Okonjo's POVs. The aftermath: neither fleet surrenders, but neither fires; a genuine negotiation begins, ugly and slow, built on admitted fault. Okonjo turns herself in, naming the forgery publicly. Ivo carries the record home. Beat: resolution without absolution; power examined and partially redeemed.

chapters.title: Someone Real
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, epilogue. Months later, Mara runs honest cargo on the rebuilt Perpetua—now a real ship that really flies—with Tomas Hale as crew, learning to remember. Dessa laughs at the paperwork; Ivo sends coded greetings. Mara keeps one rule still: never carry what isn't yours. Final beat: belonging earned, not forged.
